title: Research: masked rank-8 complex decoders are locally rigid on all P104 frame-pair punctures (no new kappa)
body:
**Status: scoped structural result (exact infinitesimal certificate) plus a seeded finite sample. No new κ, no supplier change.** Only `research/complex-p104-masked-local-rigidity/` is added; the selected record (κ = 0.001672660197076918), `upstream/` and every existing file are unchanged.

## Question

The masked (E-graph) decoder model of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717 fixes a costly part K only on the diagonal (K_ii = 4) and on orthogonal live pairs (K_ij = 0); odd entries are free and are repaired by cost-0 terms. Can masking deform the frame-pair decoders of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968, which attain the 7/13 copy ratio on P104 = P120 − F0 − F1, away from the all-pairs normal form? https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1212 proves global rank-8 rigidity on P112/P120 and lists P104 as numerical evidence only.

## Result

For P120, P112 and **every one of the 1260 frame-pair punctures**, the tangent space at K0 = 2G of {rank K ≤ 8, masked entries fixed} is exactly the tangent of the diagonal-torus orbit D(2G)D⁻¹. The solution set therefore coincides with that orbit near 2G. A masked eight-costly-term decoder close enough to 2G has the normal-form supports, so the #968 floor (cost ≥ 56, ratio ≥ 7/13 for p ≤ 24) still applies.

The certificate is exact:

- After eliminating N, the M-system has rank 7v − 63 over F_p (p = 2³¹ − 1). Since rank over F_p is at most rank over Q, the kernel is at most v + 63.
- The explicit gauge (64) and torus (v − 1) directions lie in the kernel and span 64 + v − 1.
- 66 Schreier elements fixing F0 (products of root reflections, checked) merge the 1260 frames into the 896/336/28 classes of #968; one certified representative covers each class, with full row insertion giving rank exactly 665.

Controls and sample:

- The decomposable live set D4 ⊕ D4 is rejected (its torus splits).
- 64 of 64 seeded random punctures with 24 to 80 lines pass. This is a finite sample only.
- The P112 tangent rigidity recorded in #717 D1 is reproduced by a separate exact method.

## Scope and obligations

- **Local only.** Components away from the torus orbit on P104 are not excluded (open question 1 in the README).
- **Not covered.** Nine or more costly terms (open question 2), other punctures beyond the sample, and physical copy trees, frames, restoration and hosting.
- **Inherited.** The decoder consequence uses #968's floor and its cited flat classification. All selected-record obligations remain. This is not a formal proof of multiplication, and there has been no independent human review.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-p104-masked-local-rigidity/verify.py        # ~70 s, stdlib only
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-p104-masked-local-rigidity --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-p104-masked-local-rigidity
```

Expected final line: `PASS_P104_MASKED_LOCAL_RIGIDITY: P120, P112 and all 1260 frame-pair punctures (3 classes) infinitesimally rigid at 2G; D4+D4 control rejected; seeded sample p=24..80 rigid 64/64; local only, no new kappa`.

Local runs:

- `verify.py` passes (9/9 checks) on CPython 3.13.15 and on 3.12 from a `git archive` export of the committed head.
- `research_package.py` check-only and the full 3.12 replay pass (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result`).
- `scripts/verify_selected_result.py` passes.
- `test_research_*.py` has 5 errors on this Windows host, all inside the onboarding tests' temporary repositories and unrelated to this package. Four come from the host's system `core.autocrlf=true`, and disappear with `core.autocrlf=false` for the process. The fifth uses `os.killpg`, which does not exist on Windows. Linux CI was not run.
